headline_marked: [[Cloudflare Agents SDK now supports MCP clients]] and Durable Objects on the free tier
headline: Cloudflare Agents SDK now supports MCP clients and Durable Objects on the free tier
summary: Developers can now build and deploy production AI agents at the edge without incurring Kubernetes costs, leveraging Cloudflare's globally distributed network and durable storage.
details: Cloudflare Agents SDK now supports Models Client/Server Protocol (MCP) clients and Durable Objects on its free tier. This enables developers to build and deploy production AI agents at the edge, eliminating the need for expensive Kubernetes infrastructure.

The system leverages Cloudflare Workers as a lightweight, globally distributed JavaScript/TypeScript runtime for agent logic. Durable Objects provide single-instance, strongly consistent storage for agent state, conversation history, and context, offering ACID transaction guarantees.

The MCP implementation allows agents to communicate with external services like SAP or GitHub, or to host MCP servers for other agents. This interaction enables Workers to query external services via Durable Object-stored context, perform reasoning, and return results with sub-second global latency.

Agents can be designed using two primary patterns: the MCP Agent for state persistence, ideal for maintaining conversation history or user preferences, and the Stateless Handler for simple, idempotent operations without state requirements.

While the free tier is generous, developers should monitor usage via the Cloudflare dashboard to avoid surprises. For production workloads nearing limits, upgrading to the $5/month Paid tier offers a tenfold increase in most limits.

Secure authentication for business-critical tools is crucial. This involves using scoped tokens for services like GitHub, OAuth 2.0 JWT Bearer flow for server-to-server communication, and OAuth 2.0 with SAML Bearer assertion for enterprise landscapes.

Code Mode, an underappreciated feature, significantly enhances agent effectiveness. Instead of exposing numerous individual functions, it allows agents to write and run JavaScript/TypeScript in a sandboxed environment via a single execute_code tool.

For complex integrations, like with SAP, this means exposing a single execute_abap_operation tool. This allows the agent to construct and run complex database queries or function calls through a safe abstraction layer, simplifying the LLM's context window.

Much of this development can be prototyped and tested entirely on the free tier, reducing initial infrastructure investment. The goal is to deploy agents that work reliably and scale effectively as usage grows.

headline_marked: [[Telegram Export XSS vulnerability]] affects any app generating HTML, researchers warn
headline: Telegram Export XSS vulnerability affects any app generating HTML, researchers warn
summary: A critical stored XSS vulnerability in Telegram Desktop's HTML export feature allowed silent data exfiltration and page rewriting. This bug highlights a common industry mistake in handling user-controlled data in HTML generation.
details: Security researchers discovered a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Telegram Desktop's HTML export feature that allowed silent data exfiltration. An invisible payload in a message, once exported to HTML, could execute without any user interaction.

The exploit could steal all messages, sender names, timestamps, and even local file paths from the exported chat. It also allowed attackers to completely rewrite the content of the HTML page the victim was viewing.

Disclosed on September 12, 2026, by Denis Rostilov and Aleksander Rostilov of ExPatch Vulnerability Research, the flaw was patched by Telegram in July 2026. No CVE number was assigned, and Telegram did not issue a dedicated security advisory.

The vulnerability stemmed from a single field, inline keyboard button text, being skipped during HTML escaping in the `SerializeString()` function. While other user-controlled fields were correctly escaped, this omission allowed script tags to pass through.

This incident serves as a critical reminder for any software generating HTML files. Escaping failures often occur when one field is mistakenly deemed inert or 'just a label,' emphasizing that all external data must be properly sanitized.

The bug was particularly insidious because Telegram Desktop's own UI framework rendered the malicious script tag as plain text, making it invisible to users. The vulnerability only materialized when the HTML export pipeline interpreted it as code.

This highlights a 'split-brain trust problem' where data passes through consumers with different rules, and safe treatment for one is assumed for another. This architectural pattern is a common source of similar bugs in modern applications.
